Standard: The propeller system withstands limit and ultimate load conditions as follows: Load Combinations: Load factors are applied to loads that occur within the entire flight and ground envelope IAW 7.5.2 to establish combined limit load conditions and combined ultimate load conditions. For all castings an additional 1.33 safety factor is applied to the resulting limit and ultimate load cases unless the cast material has been fully characterized IAW 7.1.3. Limit Load Conditions: Propeller system structure, when operated to limit loads within the entire flight and ground envelope, does not exhibit detrimental permanent set, damage, or reduction of life limits; and does not temporarily deflect to the extent that operation or performance is impaired, or clashing between propeller and engine, or propeller and air vehicle occurs. Limit LFs are as follows: Limit Load Factors: a. 1.0 LF for externally-applied loads (including ground and flight loads, and external flow field loads). b. 1.0 LF for thrust and thermal loads. c. 1.0 LF for internal pressure loads on cases and pressure vessels. d. 1.5 LF for internal pressure loads on controls, accessories, and externals components. Ultimate Load Conditions: Propeller system structure does not experience failure or deform to the extent of creating adverse propeller forces or unbalance, cause an uncontained engine failure or uncontained fire, or cause an engine mount system failure under ultimate load conditions. For ultimate load cases involving limit operating loads and ultimate externally-applied loads (e.g., maneuvers) the propeller system also maintains performance enabling successful recovery of the air vehicle. Ultimate LFs are as follows: Ultimate Load Factors: a. 1.5 LF for externally-applied loads (including ground and flight loads, and external flow field loads). b. 1.0 LF for thrust and thermal loads. c. 1.5 LF for internal pressure loads on cases and pressure vessels. d. 2.0 LF for centrifugal loads at maximum rated propeller rotational speed applied singly to blade hubs, blade retention systems, counterweights, and blade features associated with transition to retention features (e.g., composite blade bonded to metallic retention features). e. 2.0 LF for internal pressure loads on controls, accessories, and externals components. The non-operating propeller, including all mounted equipment and accessories, components, and operating fluids, tolerates a 4g axial, 2g lateral, and 3g vertical inertial limit load acting in any combination at the propeller CG without deformation of ground handling features or damage to the propeller; normal propeller function is unaffected after experiencing this load case. Ultimate load case is 1.5X limit load case; ground handling features do not fail under this load case. Propeller system is capable of further operation without maintenance action after operation at the maximum overspeed and overtorque limits documented in technical data. For all strength assessments, positive margins of safety exist for the range of manufacturing tolerances and operational conditions. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analyses are accomplished to define design load conditions.
(2) Analyses are accomplished using defined load conditions to verify strength and deflection capability, and system-level impacts.
(3) Analyses are accomplished to verify propeller system overspeed and overtorque capability. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Centrifugal load tests are accomplished per the conditions and success criteria as specified in 14 CFR 35.35 to verify analytical results. Tests are conducted at the maximum operating temperature or at test conditions adjusted to account for the differences between operating and test temperatures. Strain gauges and other instrumentation are used during tests to validate analysis methods. Tests are conducted progressively to limit or ultimate load conditions. Inspection of all test articles before, during, and after test verifies no unexpected interactions, failures or wear.
  (2) Lab test: Hydraulic component proof and burst tests are accomplished per the conditions and success criteria as specified in 14 CFR 35.43 to verify analytical results. Tests are conducted at the maximum operating temperature or at test conditions adjusted to account for the differences between operating and test temperatures. Strain gauges and other instrumentation are used during tests to validate analysis methods. Tests are conducted progressively to limit or ultimate load conditions. Inspection of all test articles before, during, and after test verifies no unexpected interactions, failures or wear.
  (3) Lab test: Overspeed and overtorque tests are accomplished on a whirl stand IAW JSSG-2009, Propeller Subsystem, Whirl Stand Tests, Overspeed Run paragraph or per the conditions and success criteria as specified in 14 CFR 35.41 to verify analytical results. Inspection of all test articles before, during, and after test verifies no unexpected interactions, failures or wear.
